Subject: US privacy annex — service provider scope + subprocessors (Northbridge DPA redlines)

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to send our redlines to the DPA/addendum for the US state privacy controls (CCPA/CPRA and similar state laws). Key asks from legal here:

- Confirmation that Redwood will act as a "Service Provider" (not a Controller) under CPRA and the US state privacy addendum language we provided.
- Limited-use commitments: can you confirm Redwood will only process Personal Information for the purposes set out in the Agreement and will not combine or sell data?
- Subprocessor visibility and notice: we require a living list of subprocessors and a 30-day notification for new subprocessors. For any transfers outside the US (or outside named regions) we need explicit prior consent.
- Data export/localization: can Redwood commit to keeping customer production workloads within US regions unless customer approves otherwise?

I attached our redlines (Northbridge_DPA_Redlines.pdf). Also can you provide SOC 2 evidence and current subprocessor list? We have a target of signing the addendum within two weeks if possible.

Can you confirm next steps and an owner on your side?

Thanks,
Samantha Brooks

Samantha — thanks for sending and for the clear asks. I’ve looped in Neha (Legal) and Irene (Security/Trust); Marcus from Sales will stay in the loop for procurement cadence. Quick answers and proposed next steps: 

- Service provider status: Redwood’s standard position for hosted API is to operate as a Service Provider under CPRA/US state addenda. We will not act as a controller on customer data unless a different, explicit arrangement is agreed.

- Limited use / no selling: Redwood’s DPA and internal policy prohibit use of customer content for model training or advertising. I’ll attach our privacy FAQ with the specific commitments (RNWD_privacy_FAQ.pdf).

- Subprocessor notice: we publish a subprocessor list and provide notice of additions. Our standard notice is 30 days; for any new subprocessor that would materially affect data residency or create an onward transfer we can agree to a customer notification and option to object.

- Data export/geofencing: For hosted customers we run production primarily in US regions by default; we can commit to keep Northbridge’s production tenant in the US unless you request otherwise. For stronger guarantees we recommend Dedicated / Private deployments which allow customer-controlled routing.

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha to propose specific addendum wording (we can start from your redlines).
2) Irene to provide SOC 2 snapshot and current subprocessor list.
3) Schedule a 30-minute call tomorrow or Friday to go through redlines and turnaround.
4) I’ll upload our draft DPA addendum and a suggested mutual action plan to the shared Drive.

I’ve attached RNWD_privacy_FAQ.pdf and will follow up with Neha’s notes.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: US privacy annex — proposed DPA wording and export controls

Samantha / Tessa / team —

Thanks for the redlines. I reviewed your attachment and sketched a short set of proposed edits that align with CPRA guidance and Redwood policy. Highlights below and attached is a working draft (DPA_US_Addendum_v1.docx) in the Drive.

1) "Service Provider" definition: we will accept the Service Provider designation for purposes of the CPRA/US addendum language. Proposed clause: "Redwood shall act solely as a Service Provider (or Processor, as applicable) with respect to Personal Information processed on behalf of Customer and shall process such Personal Information only for the documented purposes in the Agreement."

2) Limited Use / Training: Redwood represents that it will not use Customer Content to improve models or for advertising or profiling without explicit written consent. We can add the following: "Redwood will not use or derive models from Customer Content unless Customer provides prior written consent and signs an addendum."

3) Subprocessors: We propose a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors. For subprocessors that would materially change data residency or result in onward transfers outside the US, Redwood will provide notice and a reasonable opportunity to object. For emergency critical fixes, Redwood will provide prompt notification and document the reason for expedited onboarding.

4) Data transfers / localization: For Hosted contracts, Redwood will by default maintain Customer production instances in US regions for customers who request that restriction. Where Customer requires contractual restrictions on cross-border transfers, we offer: (a) contractual limitation preventing transfers outside the US without Customer consent; or (b) Dedicated/Private deployment with guaranteed regional hosting. We note that certain managed services (CDN, monitoring, logging) may involve metadata flow—we propose enumerating those in the addendum.

5) Evidence: you requested SOC 2 and subprocessor list — we can provide the latest SOC 2 Type II report under NDA and the current subprocessor spreadsheet; see links in Drive.

Open points we want to confirm in the call:
- Exact scope of the "no onward transfer" clause you need (all transfers vs. only production-hosting transfers).
- Whether you need vendor-level geo-fencing (i.e., blocking any subprocessors outside US) or contractual consent.

I’ve uploaded the working draft and added inline comments on your PDF. Suggest we review on a call — I’m available Thu 11–12PT or Fri 9–11PT.

—Neha
Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

Neha — thanks for the thoughtful draft. A few clarifications from our side before the call:

- "No onward transfer" should cover any production data transfers outside the US without prior written customer consent. We can accept limited exceptions for emergency security remediations provided we get notice within 48 hours.
- We prefer contractual restriction over relying on a Dedicated-only solution; most of our stack will remain hosted so we need the contract-level assurance.
- We will need SOC 2 Type II (latest) and the current subprocessor roster as deliverables before legal will sign. Can you confirm turnaround for those?

Attached is our mutual action plan with target dates (Northbridge_MAPlan.xlsx). Our legal team is aiming to have the addendum signed by 2026-08-05 if we have the SOC 2 report and subprocessor list this week.

If you can confirm availability for Thu 11:00 PT, let’s lock the call.

Thanks,
Samantha
